newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai air cargo strike ends, key shipments resume.
newsitem.headline: Thai air cargo strike ends, key shipments resume.

text.p: Nearly 1,500 Thai Airways International Plc cargo workers returned to work on Wednesday, ending a two-day strike at the international airport that had delayed vital parts for some industries.

"It's good news since most of electronic and electrical appliances manufacturers rely on imported parts. Many run just enough stocks," said Saengchai Ekapatpanich, a spokesman for the electronics and electrical appliances group of the Federation of Thai Industries.
"I heard some were forced to slow down production while waiting for imported parts," he told Reuters, adding that 80 percent of imported parts were air freighted into the country.
Several Asian airlines had also been affected by the Thai strike with movement of goods such as textiles and electronics bound for the United States and Europe delayed.
The strike was sparked by a government decision last month to launch a new Thai cargo carrier, Air Cargo Co Ltd, which the workers felt might displace their jobs.
"We resumed work after our representatives reached an agreement with the government...to halt the plan to set up a joint venture air cargo service," union spokesman Pirachat Tienson said.
He said the government had agreed not to take disciplinary action against the strikers who stopped work and staged protests in front of Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa's office.
The government had also agreed that all workers would continue in their current status as employees of Thai Airways, he added.
A government official said the workers' demands had been taken into account and the cabinet would look into the matter again at its next meeting next week.
Industry sources said that the plan to set up the new cargo carrier should go on but be undertaken on terms that were acceptable to all groups.
"Thai Airways must not be the only company that handles air cargoes here. The government should encourage competition," said another industry source.
A Thai Airways official said it was not immediately clear what the airline and the government would do with the new air cargo carrier plan.
